title: Surface supported-cohomology presentation and flag representatives
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $n\geq1$, $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$, and $S$ a Noetherian excellent normal integral strictly henselian local scheme of dimension $2$, with closed point $s$ and $\ell$ invertible [def-exc-excellent-ring, def-weil-pbc-normal-ring, def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Use ordinary etale cohomology and closed supports [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-pur-etale-derived-supported-sections], and the twists and immediate transitions of [def-per-potential-dualizing-complex]. There exists a projective birational morphism $p:S'\to S$, an isomorphism away from $s$, with $S'$ regular and $E=p^{-1}(s)_{\mathrm{red}}$ a strict normal-crossing union of regular proper curves $D_1,\ldots,D_N$, $N\geq1$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-regular-scheme]. The intersection graph of these curves is connected. A strict normal crossing here means that at most two components pass through a point and that at an intersection they are defined by the two elements of a regular system of parameters [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. There are canonical maps giving an exact sequence
$$\bigoplus_{i<j}\ \bigoplus_{z\in D_i\cap D_j}\Lambda\xrightarrow{\partial}\bigoplus_{i=1}^N\Lambda e_i\xrightarrow{\epsilon}H^4_s(S,\Lambda(2))\longrightarrow0,$$
where $\partial(e_z)=[\kappa(z):\kappa(s)](e_i-e_j)$; all these residue degrees are invertible in $\Lambda$. Under $H^4_s(S,\Lambda(2))\cong H^4_E(S',\Lambda(2))$, $\epsilon(e_i)$ is the enlargement of support of $[\kappa(z):\kappa(s)]^{-1}\operatorname{Cl}_{z\hookrightarrow S'}$ for any closed point $z\in D_i$, where $\operatorname{Cl}$ is the regular Gysin class [lem-per-absolute-gysin-purity].
For any codimension-one point $y$ of $S$, one can choose such a resolution on which the strict transform of its reduced closure is its normalized strictly henselian trait. If it meets $E$ at $z\in D_i$, then the composite of the two normalized immediate transitions along any geometric flag $\bar\eta\rightsquigarrow\bar y\rightsquigarrow\bar s$ sends $1$ to $\epsilon(e_i)$. Any two such resolutions admit a common dominating resolution. Each dominating morphism is an isomorphism over an open of the target whose complement has dimension zero, so this open meets an exceptional component in a nonempty open containing a closed point. For a morphism between two of them that is an isomorphism over a closed point of the exceptional curves, pullback identifies the normalized point Gysin classes and hence their enlargements of support.
